summary: Round 25 plan check, 28 Sep ~10:40Z. Probe 50 (exp85a) is still PENDING at the 10:13:17Z header; it should turn terminal at ~12:03-12:50Z (submitted 05:02:30Z, L 7.0-7.8 h). We are #153 at 0.957, 16th of 42 in that block. No E10 trigger (every public notebook is <= 0.953) and no new discussion posts since 06:30Z. Amendment A (probe 51 = exp87a under R+, else exp83c) is consistent and both dummies PASS. Nine gaps remain. (1) Probe 51's own read rule against exp79a is not pre-registered. (2) The W4/29 Sep plan now sits in four overlapping texts that contradict each other: the 10:16Z exp75 proposal hits the R21-A3 NO-GO and the LIFT-SPLIT kinds, the AMEND 3 SEC clause can never fire, and the knob arms are still cut off the non-CI base. (3) '09:30Z' is too late for a morning CI file (FINALS READ 19:00Z). (4) The exp75 dummy fails runtime rule v2 as logged. (5) A {exp79a, exp75} pair puts CI in both finals. The lab shows one clip at -0.021, and JT's best+neighbour pair {exp79a, exp70g} needs no slot. (6) The CI_lo 2.2 h model is above the measured same-batch CI time (1.88-2.18 h). (7) exp86c fails the literal R24-A4 gate, and the exp88c gate is not pre-registered. (8) The -m token decides the family and session liveness at 12:15-13:00Z matters. (9) There is no fallback if the user does not re-tick (#37+#38 = 0.954/0.953).

Amendment A says which file goes, but not how its display is coded against the new best, exp79a 0.957. Without that rule, a 0.957 read is ambiguous. It could mean a non-additive stop of K+CI, or SEC closed, or a tie. The W4 freeze at 23:30Z needs that code.

findings.action: Before 50 is terminal (by ~12:00Z), append a line 'PROBE 51 READ RULE (pre-score; header <time> shows 56629533 PENDING)'. S0 = a fresh LB download taken at 50's terminal header (count 52). S1 = the first download showing count 53. Probe 51 is then the only pending ref, so k is clean. Codes against exp79a: display >= 0.958 -> '+' (new best). 0.957 with an attributable UP -> '+' (new unrounded best). 0.957 with no UP -> '0'. <= 0.956 -> '-'. For exp87a, K '+' and C '+' with a '0'/'-' stack -> NON-ADDITIVE (AMEND 2 (3)): no further K+CI stacks, and V_pub stays exp79a. For exp83c, '+' makes SEC '+' on the best base (finals-eligible only after the user answers Q3), and '0'/'-' closes SEC for 29 Sep. Log L with the CI-RAN rule, sibling = exp85a (under R+) or exp70g (exp81 is unscored).

With the measured CI latency, 09:30Z reads at 18:46-18:57Z, 3-14 min before the FINALS READ at ~19:00Z. With the logged CI band of 9.4-10.9 h it reads as late as 20:24Z, after the 20:00Z tick. A morning stack of 'night winners + CI' can only use the 00:05Z non-CI read (it lands ~07:05-07:55Z). The 00:45/01:25Z reads land at 07:45-09:15Z, too late for a CI file.

findings.what: The safetail_ci insertion-gate line ('did NOT fire' iff L_hi <= 10.2 h) rests on a CI_lo = 2.2 h model from 27 Sep, which is above the measured CI time. Against the same-batch sibling, CI took (1.88, 2.18] h. So a CI read with L_hi in (9.88, 10.2] h may have had its insertion skipped by the 8.0 h DIVINS deadline, yet it would be coded as clean. This matters for probe 51 (~22:00-23:30Z) and for any 29 Sep CI file.

findings.what: Probe 51 submit hygiene and liveness. The ledger reads the family from the FIRST exp token of the -m description (tools/runtime_ledger.py EXP_TOKEN / family_of). A text such as 'probe 51: FULL exp70g + K + CI (exp87a)' would file a CI file as safetail (9.5 h), and its normal ~9.4 h latency would then be misread. Probe 50 should be terminal at 12:03-12:50Z. If the file goes at 14:00Z, a CI file reads by up to 23:27Z, which leaves no margin before the 23:30Z freeze.
